output.summary: An annual flowering herb native to south-central China and Tibet, common buckwheat has red stems, arrow-shaped leaves and pink-and-white flowers. Its sharply three-angled, starchy seeds are eaten like cereal even though the plant is not a grass; buckwheat can trigger severe allergies.
output.edibilityNote: The hulled, starchy seeds are eaten as groats or flour in foods such as porridge and noodles; severe allergic reactions are reported.
